symptom: `mxcli exec`: a statement that fails at write time (after the pre-check passed) leaves every earlier statement written — a created module and entity stay, and a `drop` ahead of the failing `create` is not undone
cause: exec applied statements one at a time, each landing on disk as it ran, with no way back; the only all-or-nothing gate was the pre-check, which cannot predict write-time failures (a property the project's Mendix version cannot store, a widget that does not build)
file: `modelsdk/mpr/journal.go` (`BeginJournal`, `journalDB` via `guardWrite`, `journalFile` at the four mprcontents write/delete sites in `writer_core.go`); `cmd/mxcli/cmd_exec.go` (`runScriptAtomically`)
insight: A before-image journal, not a write buffer: buffering would have to make inserts and deletes visible to later reads in the run (deferral only holds updates, writer_deferred.go), while journaling leaves the write path — reconcile, elision, identity carry — exactly as it was and only copies each file before the run first touches it. `guardWrite` is already the choke point every write passes before it changes anything, so the .mpr copy is taken there. Rollback must run after the executor is closed: a deferred access-rule write lands at Close, and the .mpr is replaced under SQLite. Test hashes the whole project tree INCLUDING directories (a created unit's XX/YY dirs must go too) on both a v1 and a v2 fixture; control: the same script minus the failing statement must change the tree
